text:
sasha: noticing a p95 token latency spike on a few fleets when FIFO eviction is enabled + long-context workloads. looks like paging churn but not sure about correctness vs scheduling.

jason: saw that earlier today, very short bursts ~3-7s where tail latency doubles. repro on canary VMs?

sasha: reprod on canary-3 with config: `kv.eviction.policy=fifo`, `kv.hotset.watermark=0.72`, long_ctx=true. spike aligns with large prefix reuse patterns.

maria: any kernel selection differences around those times? maybe quantized kernels amplify paging cost.

sasha: good call — profile shows a rise in time spent in `kv_page_swap()` + a jump in context-switches inside the eviction worker. stacktrace snippet: ```
kv_page_swap+0x84
evicter_worker+0x120
memmgr_handle_page+0x3f
```

oliver: values from perf sampling: `cpu_cycles: +42%`, `cache-misses: +18%`, `syscalls (futex): +260%` during spike window. looks like eviction worker fights request threads.

tina: that futex surge smells like a contention on the eviction queue. FIFO reinserts might be causing rewalks. did we recently change reinsertion semantics?

jason: we changed FIFO reinsert to requeue at tail instead of bumping timestamp in 2.3.1 — intended to reduce reorder noise. could be causing repeated page touches for warm keys.

sasha: exact timeline: before change p50/p95 stable; after change we see periodic microbursts under bursty allocs. I ran a small microbench: 50 clients long-contexts (~8k tokens) sending interleaved requests; enabling FIFO caused KV reuse to drop by ~22% and page outs to increase.

perf-bot: automated regression test results attached: `kv_reuse_longctx_test` failed on fifo branch (p95 +1.9x) — see /ci/kv_regressions/5897654321.

maria: can you paste the short repro command? I'll spin a profile with kernels pinned.

sasha: repro command: ```
./bench_runner --clients=50 --ctx_len=8192 --pattern=interleaved-prefix --kv-policy=fifo --duration=180
perf record -o /tmp/perf.data ./bench_runner ...
```

oliver: after looking at traces, eviction worker iterates the slab list and issues `page_evict()` which blocks on io when pager is active. FIFO behavior causes older-but-still-warm entries to be cycled out and re-requested quickly, causing ping-pong. LRU had a softer tail.

tina: hypothesis: FIFO reinserts + aggressive hotset watermark + batching heuristics that coalesce KV writes are interacting badly. when batch size dips, kernel selection switches to a narrow-kernel path with higher per-token cost, making eviction latency proportionally worse.

jason: so several levers: 1) reduce hotset watermark to avoid early paging, 2) change reinsert semantics to bump a cheap recency token, 3) short-term disable FIFO under long-context workload detection.

sasha: quick mitigation I tried on canary-3: set `kv.hotset.watermark=0.85` + `kv.eviction.reinsert_mode=bump` and the spikes disappeared in 3 runs. p95 back to baseline.

maria: nice. can we add a circuit: if ctx_len > 6k && fifo_enabled -> auto-fallback to `reinsert_mode=bump`? we should be careful about regressing FIFO improvements on other workloads.

oliver: agree. add telemetry tag so we can measure effect: `kv.policy.fallback_reason=long_ctx_reuse_loss` and track reuse-% and page-outs.

sasha: action items: 1) olive/oliver to write a focused e2e test that reproduces the ping-pong with FIFO under long contexts (owner: oliver) 2) maria to run kernel-pin experiments to see if narrow-kernel path amplifies impact (owner: maria) 3) jason to propose a safe fallback rule and add telemetry (owner: jason) 4) tina to draft a short postmortem snippet for release notes if we ship fallback (owner: tina).

jason: I can PR a config gating + telemetry today; will add runtime flag `kv.policy.fifo.long_ctx_fallback=true` default false.

perf-bot: regression triage created: #EV-2319 with labels [kv-cache, perf, regression, fifo].

maria: timeline: let's get tests + kernels profiling by EOD tomorrow, then decide on hotfix.

sasha: thanks all — keeping thread here for logs. if anyone finds conflicting traces, drop them in this thread.

jason: logging note: I also added a short metric `kv.eviction.loop_duration_ms` to the canary; should help correlate.

oliver: uploaded perf flamegraphs to s3://redwood-perf/5897654321/flame.svg

tina: one more thought — check batching heuristic: if we let the batcher hold onto a tiny batch instead of switching kernel immediately, we may avoid the kernel micro-path that magnifies eviction cost. adding to the experiment queue.

sasha: cool. I'll follow up with raw trace links and heap profiles here once available.
